title: Listening cannot resume after its playback service is destroyed
symptom: The controller can retain a playback session while the Service and engine no longer exist. Continue then produces no sound; a cold foreground-service continuation can also miss Android's foreground-promotion deadline.
root_cause: The old recovery path depended on an in-memory queue and prepared engine, with no independent durable listening checkpoint or complete cold-resume initialization. Foreground promotion happened after potentially suspending preparation.
fix: Persist listening checkpoints independently of reading positions and rebuild only the current and next chapter from the saved location.
Promote the Service before storage/model suspension, reflect destruction as paused, and give preparation a bounded failure state.
Only actual playback completion advances the checkpoint; stale operations and callbacks cannot publish into a later session.
evidence: ReaderTtsBackgroundPlaybackTest.resumeAfterServiceDisappearsRebuildsAtLastCompletedBoundary failed before the change: no replacement engine/continuation, followed by ForegroundServiceDidNotStartInTimeException on cold resume. It passes after the change with a real Service stop and reconstruction.

ListeningProgressStoreTest passes six real-file cases. The Service test uses a controlled engine to isolate lifecycle order; host-process termination, actual long playback and Xiaomi background behavior are separately tracked in the 2026-09-20 offline-listening plan.

On the final v3 Xiaomi 15 Ultra, pause then host force-stop terminates PID29380. Normal reopening creates PID15510 without automatic playback or a media session; the listening checkpoint file remains byte-identical at chapter2/1282. Explicit continuation produces actual captured audio at offset1285, follows that position in the reader and advances the checkpoint. Direct source inspection confirms the three skipped UTF-16 characters are newline plus two ideographic spaces.
impact: This closes the identified recovery defect. It does not establish the sole cause of the user's several-minute Xiaomi screen-off interruption or mark that device scenario accepted.
